ABOUT US


FiftyFive Technologies is a Technology-empowered IT outsourcing company founded in 2016 in Jaipur,
Rajasthan. We are relentlessly broadening our horizons and we have offices in Jaipur, Gurugram, Indore,
London (United Kingdom), Dubai (UAE). As a Multinational Corporation, we are stretching ourselves to
the prominent business locations across the globe.

As an outsourcing company we provide a diverse array of consulting & development services to the top
HNI customers operating in IoT, AI, Gaming, Energy, FinTech, Travel & Manufacturing, etc sectors.

Having launched our own games, we are now positioned as a progressive gaming company with a strong
product portfolio. This marks the evolution of our product-driven side, focused on creativity, scalability,
and global reach.

FiftyFive Technologies is not operating as an organization full of Work Zombies giving tones of work.

Instead, we are a family, we want to create fun-loving stories at the workplace with flexible hours, a
hybrid structure, and a jovial environment. In order to avoid beating around the bush, “We are a culturally
inclined Family”.

Our Vision
At FiftyFive Technologies, we’re not just about tech; we’re about creating a vibrant, people-first
culture that celebrates work-life harmony. We envision a workplace where every team member feels
like a valued part of the FiftyFive Family, working in an open and dynamic environment where
innovation thrives.

Our goal is to build a company powered by cutting-edge technology and extraordinary people—a
company that propels businesses into the future while prioritizing trust, transparency, and satisfaction
for both clients and employees.

We’re committed to uncovering hidden talent from every corner of India, especially from smaller
cities where big dreams often face limited opportunities. Our vision is to provide a platform where
talent can shine, careers can thrive, and boundaries are redefined.



Our Mission
We’re on a mission to grow our family to 500+ exceptional individuals, all united by a passion for
creating outstanding solutions. To achieve this, we’re not just scaling heights—we’re redefining them.

From launching our groundbreaking in-house gaming product to rolling out a state-of-the-art travel
app, we’re paving the way for innovation. As we aim to become the go-to game development service
provider for global companies, our focus remains steadfast: enabling businesses to evolve with
technology and delivering unparalleled value every single day.

Join us as we push the boundaries of what’s possible—together.

Values we Patronize


Care for Our Planet and Society

To us, the planet is more than just a home—it’s our shared responsibility. We are deeply committed to
nurturing our ecosystem and giving back to the society that sustains us.



Care for Our People

At FiftyFive Technologies, our people are our greatest strength—the foundation and the force behind
everything we achieve. We are passionate about their growth, well-being, and success, fostering an
environment where they can thrive.



Care for Our Customers

Our customers are the heartbeat of our journey. We are dedicated to their success, walking with them
through every step of their product development and transformation. Their victories are ours too,
fueling our shared growth and innovation.



Care for Technology

Our belief in technology goes beyond the surface. Guided by our tagline, “Culture Beyond Tech,” we
embrace technology as a transformative force for good, enabling people to experience its full potential
and shaping a better tomorrow.

EMPLOYEE BENEFITS



Introduction
An employee shall be entitled to the benefits provided by the Company upon joining. However,
FiftyFive Technologies reserves the right to amend, modify, or withdraw any benefits at its sole
discretion, in accordance with business requirements and applicable laws.



   1. Salary Benefit:

      The salary of the month is credited every 1st of the month if in case there is a holiday on the
      same date, the salary gets credited on the next working day.



   2. Health Insurance:

      FiftyFive currently provides individuals, spouses, and their children health insurance benefits
      for eligible full-time employees. FiftyFive presently pays the individual insurance premium for
      all its employees.



   3. Accidental Insurance:

      FiftyFive also provides individual accidental insurance benefits for eligible full-time
      employees. FiftyFive presently pays the individual insurance premium for all its employees.



   4. Reimbursement Expense:

      Reimbursement is authorized for reasonable and necessary expenses incurred in carrying out
      job responsibilities. Mileage or transportation, parking fees, business telephone calls, and meal
      costs when required to attend a luncheon or banquet, are all illustrative of reasonable and
      necessary expenses.



   5. Meal Benefit:

      FiftyFive provides lunch facilities for employees. Additionally, a full-time coffee/tea machine is
      available within the office premises to ensure employees can refresh themselves and stay
      comfortable during work hours.

6. Special Friday:

   FiftyFive treats Friday as a special day of the week wherein employees get the opportunity to
   enjoy themselves through outdoor/indoor games, activities, and parties including a special
   meal.



7. Team Quarterly Surprises:

   A special surprise including trips, activities, parties, and fitness programs is organized on behalf
   of the company on a quarterly basis to create a healthy and friendly working culture among the
   employees of the company.



8. Certification Policy:

   To continue and promote learning within the organization, we are formally introducing
   FiftyFive Technologies learning program. We are introducing a Certification Policy.

   Employees can go for various certifications relevant to their current profile and enhance their
   skill set. On successful completion, the cost of certifications will be reimbursed by the
   company.


   Rules:

         1. Employees who are availing this benefit should be confirmed employee only and
            while opting this course benefit, they should serve the company for at least 12
            months more.

         2. If an employee avails reimbursement for any certification and he/she resigns from the
            organization after or during the period availing the benefit, he/she has to bear the
            cost of certification which will hence be adjusted in the full and final settlement.

         3. Candidates can only opt for certification relevant to the skill set required as per
            candidate’s work allocation or aligned with organization goals.

         4. Certification requirements and reimbursement must be approved by the reporting
            manager.

         5. To start with each candidate can avail reimbursement of up to INR 40000 per
            financial year.

         6. Reimbursement is subject to completion of certification only, registration or
            attending training sessions or courses will not be considered for reimbursement.

9. Employee Bonus Clause

  FiftyFive Technologies offers several types of bonuses to its employees. Please refer to the
  explanation of each type of bonus mentioned below:

          A) Performance Bonus: Performance Bonus means the performance bonus in respect
             of an individual's performance. A performance bonus is a form of additional
             compensation paid to an employee as a reward for achieving specific goals or
             hitting predetermined targets. Hence will be payable according to the terms and
             conditions decided by the company. In the event of you resigning from the services
             of the Company on your own accord within the duration, the bonus will be
             considered as NIL.



          B) Company Performance Bonus: A company performance bonus is a financial
             reward given to employees based on the overall success and profitability of the
             company, often tied to achieving specific performance goals or benchmarks. Unlike
             individual bonuses, which are typically linked to an employee's achievements or
             role-specific targets, a performance bonus reflects the collective effort and
             accomplishments of the entire organization. This type of bonus encourages
             employees to work toward shared objectives and contributes to a unified company
             culture.
             Performance bonuses are usually awarded annually or quarterly, depending on
             company policy, and may be based on metrics such as revenue growth, cost
             savings, productivity, or customer satisfaction scores. By sharing in the company's
             success, employees feel recognized for their contributions and motivated to
             continue driving positive results for the business. In the event of you resigning
             from the services of the Company on your own accord within the duration, the
             bonus will be considered as NIL.



          C) Retention Bonus: A retention bonus is a targeted one-time payment or reward
             outside of an employee's regular salary that is offered as an incentive to keep a key
             employee on the job. Terms of a retention bonus agreement may also include non-
             disclosure terms, assignment right terms, and reimbursement terms should retention
             bonus installment payments be made. Hence will be payable according to the terms
             and conditions decided by the company. In the event of you resigning from the
             services of the Company on your own accord within the duration, the bonus will be
             considered as NIL.



  Note: Terms and Conditions are accordingly applied for the above bonus components point

Documented Information Control Procedure

                             Document Release Notice


   This FiftyFive Technologies Policy on documented information control is released for use in
              FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited with effect from 01 January 2026.

This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change at
                                any time as per the company policy.

           Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
          Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

1. Purpose
The purpose of this Documented Information Control Procedure is to establish guidelines for
managing and controlling documented information within FiftyFive Technologies. This procedure
ensures that all documented information is accurate, accessible, secure, and compliant with relevant
standards and regulations.




2. Scope
This procedure applies to all documented information created, received, or maintained by FiftyFive
Technologies. It covers all forms of documented information, including physical documents,
electronic files, and records.



3. Definitions
    •   Documented Information: Information that is required to be controlled and maintained to
        ensure the effectiveness of the organization's processes. This includes policies, procedures,
        work instructions, records, and other types of documents.

    •   Control: Measures taken to ensure that documented information is accurate, accessible,
        secure, and properly managed throughout its lifecycle.




4. Procedure
    4.1 Document Creation and Approval

        •   Creation:

                ❖ Create documents according to established templates and formats to ensure
                  consistency and compliance.

                ❖ Ensure documents are accurate, clear, and complete, with all required information
                  included.

        •   Approval:

                ❖ Submit documents for review and approval by designated personnel.

                ❖ Obtain formal approval before finalizing and distributing documents. Record
                  approval with the name, date, and signature or electronic equivalent of the
                  approver.

4.2 Document Identification and Revision Control

   •   Identification:

           ❖ Assign a unique identifier to each document, including a title, version number,
             and date of issue.

           ❖ Use a document numbering system to facilitate easy tracking and retrieval.

   •   Revision Control:

           ❖ Implement a revision control system to manage updates to documents.

           ❖ Document all changes, including the reason for changes, date of revision, and the
             individual responsible for the update.

           ❖ Ensure that obsolete versions are archived or removed from active circulation to
             prevent confusion.



4.3 Document Distribution and Accessibility

   •   Distribution:

           ❖ Distribute documents to relevant personnel based on their role and
             responsibilities.

           ❖ Use secure methods to distribute sensitive or confidential documents to prevent
             unauthorized access.

   •   Accessibility:

           ❖ Ensure that documents are readily accessible to authorized users, including
             physical access and electronic access through appropriate systems.

           ❖ Implement access controls to restrict document access to authorized personnel
             only.

4.4 Document Storage and Protection

   •   Storage:

          ❖ Store physical documents in secure locations that protect them from damage,
            loss, or unauthorized access.

          ❖ Store electronic documents in secure systems with backup and recovery
            capabilities.

   •   Protection:

          ❖ Implement security measures to protect the integrity and confidentiality of
            documents, such as encryption, password protection, and physical security
            controls.

4.5 Document Review and Update

   •   Review:

          ❖ Schedule regular reviews of documents to ensure they remain current and
            accurate. Review periods should be specified for each document or based on
            changes in processes or regulations.

   •   Update:

          ❖ Update documents as necessary to reflect changes, correct errors, or improve
            clarity. Ensure that updates are approved and communicated to relevant
            personnel.

          ❖ Archive or appropriately handle outdated documents to avoid confusion and
            ensure that only current versions are in use.

4.6 Document Retention and Disposal

   •   Retention:

          ❖ Define retention periods for different types of documents based on legal,
            regulatory, and organizational requirements.

          ❖ Ensure that documents are retained for the required duration and are easily
            retrievable during this time.

   •   Disposal:

          ❖ Dispose of documents that are no longer needed according to established
            procedures.

          ❖ Use secure disposal methods for confidential or sensitive documents, such as
            shredding physical documents and securely deleting electronic files.

5. Roles and Responsibilities

       5.1 Document Control Manager

               •   Oversight: Manage and oversee the document control process, ensuring
                   compliance with this procedure.

               •   Support: Provide guidance and support for document management activities
                   across the organization.

       5.2 Department Managers

               •   Implementation: Ensure adherence to document control procedures within their
                   departments. Monitor compliance and address any issues.

               •   Review: Participate in the review and update of documents relevant to their areas
                   of responsibility.

       5.3 Employees

               •   Compliance: Follow established procedures for document creation, distribution,
                   storage, and disposal. Report any issues or discrepancies related to documents to
                   their supervisors or the Document Control Manager.




6. Policy Compliance and Enforcement
6.1 Compliance

               •   Regulatory Requirements: Ensure document control practices comply with
                   applicable regulations and industry standards.

               •   Internal Audits: Conduct audits to assess compliance with this procedure and
                   identify areas for improvement.

6.2 Enforcement

               •   Disciplinary Actions: Failure to adhere to this procedure may result in
                   disciplinary action. Ensure enforcement is consistent with company policies and
                   legal requirements.




7. Procedure Review and Updates
Review this procedure annually or as needed to ensure it remains effective and current. Communicate
any updates to all employees and stakeholders.

Nonconformity and Corrective Action Procedure

                              Document Release Notice

This FiftyFive Technologies Policy on nonconformity and corrective action procedure is released for
            use in FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited with effect from 01 January 2026.

This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change at
                                any time as per the company policy.


            Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
           Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

1. Purpose
The purpose of this Nonconformity and Corrective Action Procedure is to define the process for
identifying, documenting, and addressing nonconformities within FiftyFive Technologies. The
procedure ensures that corrective actions are taken to eliminate the causes of nonconformities and
prevent their recurrence.



2. Scope
This procedure applies to all departments and processes within FiftyFive Technologies. It covers
nonconformities related to products, services, processes, and compliance with internal and external
requirements.



3. Definitions
    •   Nonconformity: A deviation from specified requirements or standards that affects the quality
        or compliance of a product, service, or process.

    •   Corrective Action: Actions taken to eliminate the causes of nonconformities to prevent their
        recurrence.

    •   Preventive Action: Actions taken to eliminate the causes of potential nonconformities to
        prevent their occurrence.



4. Procedure
    4.1 Identification of Nonconformities

        •   Detection: Identify nonconformities through various means, including inspections,
            audits, customer feedback, or employee reports.

        •   Documentation: Document the nonconformity in a Nonconformity Report (NCR),
            including details of the issue, the affected area, and any immediate actions taken.

    4.2 Evaluation of Nonconformities

        •   Impact Assessment: Evaluate the impact of the nonconformity on product quality,
            service delivery, or compliance. Determine whether the nonconformity affects customer
            satisfaction or poses a risk to the organization.

        •   Root Cause Analysis: Conduct a root cause analysis to identify the underlying causes of
            the nonconformity.

4.3 Corrective Action Planning

   •   Action Plan: Develop a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) to address the root causes of the
       nonconformity. The plan should include specific actions, responsible individuals, and
       deadlines for completion.

   •   Approval: Obtain approval for the Corrective Action Plan from relevant stakeholders or
       management.

4.4 Implementation of Corrective Actions

   •   Execution: Implement the corrective actions as outlined in the plan. Ensure that actions
       are carried out effectively and according to the specified timeline.

   •   Communication: Communicate the corrective actions to all affected parties and provide
       any necessary training or support.

4.5 Verification of Effectiveness

   •   Follow-Up: Verify the effectiveness of the corrective actions by monitoring the affected
       processes or products. Ensure that the nonconformity has been resolved and that no new
       issues have arisen.

   •   Review: Conduct a review to assess whether the corrective actions have achieved the
       desired outcomes and prevented recurrence of the nonconformity.

4.6 Documentation and Records

   •   Record Keeping: Maintain records of nonconformities, corrective actions, and their
       effectiveness. Ensure that records are accessible for review and auditing purposes.

   •   Reporting: Report the status and outcomes of corrective actions to management and
       relevant stakeholders.

4.7 Preventive Actions (if applicable)

   •   Identification: Identify potential nonconformities and areas for improvement through
       risk assessments or other proactive measures.

   •   Action Planning: Develop and implement preventive actions to address potential issues
       before they result in nonconformities.

   •   Monitoring: Monitor the effectiveness of preventive actions and adjust as necessary to
       ensure continued effectiveness.

5. Roles and Responsibilities
    5.1 Quality Manager

        •   Oversight: Oversee the nonconformity and corrective action process, including the
            review and approval of corrective action plans.

        •   Support: Provide guidance and support for identifying nonconformities and
            implementing corrective actions.

    5.2 Department Managers

        •   Implementation: Ensure that corrective actions are implemented within their respective
            departments and that affected personnel are informed.

        •   Monitoring: Monitor the effectiveness of corrective actions and report any issues to the
            Quality Manager.

    5.3 Employees

        •   Reporting: Report nonconformities and potential issues to their supervisors or designated
            personnel.

        •   Compliance: Follow corrective action plans and contribute to the resolution of
            nonconformities.




6. Policy Compliance and Enforcement
    6.1 Compliance

        •   Regulatory Requirements: Ensure that corrective actions comply with applicable laws,
            regulations, and industry standards.

        •   Internal Audits: Conduct regular audits to assess compliance with this procedure and
            identify areas for improvement.

    6.2 Enforcement

        •   Disciplinary Actions: Failure to adhere to this procedure may result in disciplinary
            action, up to and including termination of employment. Ensure that actions are consistent
            with company policies and legal requirements.




7. Procedure Review and Updates
This procedure will be reviewed annually or as needed to ensure it remains current and effective.
Updates will be communicated to all employees and relevant stakeholders.

FiftyFive Policy - Intern Training Period
                               Document Release Notice


This FiftyFive Technologies Policy on trainee period is released for use in FiftyFive Technologies Pvt
                             Limited with effect from 01 January 2026.

This document is subject to FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited Procedure and subject to change any
                                  time as per the company policy.

             Approved By: Jyothi Sharma (CEO-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt. Limited)
            Approved By: Sanchi Saxena (Head HR-FiftyFive Technologies Pvt Limited)

Introduction


Intern Training Period

FiftyFive Technologies has a mandatory Intern Training Period that every Intern joining the
organization is required to undergo. This Intern Training Period enables the Intern to clearly
understand their role, goals, responsibilities, and performance expectations aligned with FiftyFive’s
standards. Upon successful completion of the Training Period, the Intern may be confirmed as a
permanent employee, subject to satisfactory performance and business requirements.



Purpose

The purpose of this policy is to ensure that every Intern joining FiftyFive Technologies undergoes a
structured Intern Training Period that helps them understand their roles, responsibilities, goals, and
expected performance standards. This policy aims to facilitate smooth onboarding, assess the Intern’s
suitability for the role, align individual performance with organizational objectives, and ensure
readiness for confirmation as a permanent employee upon successful completion of the Intern
Training Period.



Applicability

This policy is applicable to all Learning & Industry Exposure, Paid & Unpaid Internship and Training,
Student Internship employees of FiftyFive Technologies.

This policy is not applicable to experienced employees of FiftyFive Technologies who possess a
minimum of six (6) months of prior work experience at the time of joining the organization.



Definition of Trainees

For the purpose of this policy, Intern Trainees include individuals engaged under Learning & Industry
Exposure programs, Paid or Unpaid Internships, Training programs, and Student Internship programs.
This definition also covers interns recruited from MBA, B.Tech, or other educational institutions, as
well as those engaged through external sources.

Provisions

Paid Internships:
   •   Employment Status and Termination

       During your tenure as an intern employee, your services shall be treated as “probationary”
       and can be terminated anytime without any notice period or without assigning any reasons.
       This decision rests entirely with the Company, and the decision of the Company shall be
       final and binding on you in all respects.



   •   Stipend Payment

       As a gesture of support, the Company may, at its sole discretion, pay a monthly stipend to
       Interns during the Intern Training Period. The decision to offer a stipend shall be based on
       the Intern’s performance, role requirements, and business needs, and shall rest entirely with
       the Company. The decision of the Company shall be final and binding in all respects.

             ❖ The stipend, if applicable, shall be paid monthly and will be inclusive of all
               applicable statutory deductions.
             ❖ The stipend structure may vary based on business requirements, role expectations,
               and the profile of the Intern/Trainee.
             ❖ The Company reserves the absolute right to revise, modify, suspend, or withdraw
               the stipend structure at any time, without prior notice.

   •   Exit Process for “Interns”

       It is hereby clarified and understood that during the probation period, the Company invests
       significant time, effort, and resources in training and developing the employee, thereby
       adding value at its own cost. The stipend or remuneration paid during this period is not
       intended to be full compensation for such investment. Accordingly, if the employee chooses
       to resign or discontinue services before the completion of the intern training period from the
       date of joining, the employee shall be required to serve a notice period of two (2) months.
       This condition shall be legally binding on the employee.

       In the event of non-compliance with the notice period requirement, the Company reserves
       the right to initiate appropriate legal action as deemed necessary. The employee shall be held
       liable for any fees, costs, expenses, or losses incurred by the Company as a result of such
       premature separation.

•   Leave Policy

    1. Exam Leave Policy: Interns who are currently pursuing their Graduation or Post-
       Graduation are eligible to apply for Exam Leave. To avail of this leave, Interns must
       submit an official examination date sheet issued by their respective college or university
       as supporting proof via email to their reporting manager, with the HR team marked in
       CC. The leave request must be submitted at least fifteen (15) days prior to the
       commencement of the examinations.

         Exam Leave shall be approved strictly in accordance with the actual examination dates
         mentioned in the submitted date sheet. Any additional leave required for examination
         preparation shall be subject to prior approval from the reporting manager.

    2.   Casual Leave: Every Intern is eligible for six (6) leaves during the Intern Training
         Period. Interns may apply for leave directly through the KEKA portal.

    Leave entitlement shall commence from the date of joining and shall be credited at the
    rate of one (1) leave per month during the Training Period.

    Upon confirmation as a full-time employee, the total annual leave entitlement shall be
    twelve (12) leaves, inclusive of the six (6) leaves already accrued during the Training
    Period. The remaining six (6) leaves shall continue to be credited as per the Company’s
    Full-Time Employee Leave Policy.



•   Performance Review

    During the Intern Training Period, the Company will closely monitor the Intern’s
    performance, work quality, work attitude, and availability. Failure to meet the Company’s
    performance standards or behavioral expectations may result in the Company taking
    appropriate action, including continuation, extension, or discontinuation of the training
    engagement, as deemed necessary.

    Performance reviews shall be conducted on a monthly or quarterly basis, aligned with the
    Intern’s date of joining. Subject to satisfactory performance and suitability for the role, the
    Intern may be considered for confirmation as a full-time employee upon successful
    completion of a minimum of six (6) months of the Training Period with the Company.

•   Company Assets Policy for Interns

    Paid Interns may be provided with Company assets such as laptops, mobile devices,
    software, or other equipment required for their work. These assets remain in the property of
    the Company and must be used solely for work-related purposes. Interns are responsible
    for their care, maintenance, and security, and any loss, damage, or misuse may make the
    Intern financially liable as per the assets policy of the company.

    All assets must be returned in full and in working condition upon completion of the
    internship, termination, or upon request. Interns must also ensure that any data or
    information accessed through Company assets remains confidential, and any breach of this
    policy may result in disciplinary action or legal consequences.



•   Misconduct or Breach of Service Conditions

    In the event that the Intern is found to have engaged in any misconduct, breached any of the
    Company’s service conditions, or committed any act which, in the opinion of the Company,
    is prejudicial to the interests of the Company, the Company reserves the right to terminate
    the engagement with immediate effect and without prior notice.

    The Company’s decision regarding the occurrence or determination of any such misconduct
    or breach shall be final and binding. The Intern shall not be entitled to question or
    challenge the same on any grounds whatsoever.



•   Full-Time Employment Disclaimer

    Completion of the Internship/Intern Training Period does not guarantee, confer, or create
    any right or entitlement to full-time employment with the Company.

    Upon successful completion of the program, the Company may, at its sole discretion,
    evaluate the Intern’s performance, skills, qualifications, and alignment with business
    requirements.

    Subject to the availability of a suitable role and internal approvals, the Company may
    consider offering full-time employment.

    The Intern/Trainee expressly understands and agrees that:

        •   The Company is under no obligation to offer full-time employment.

        •   No assurance, promise, or commitment—whether express or implied—has been
            made regarding permanent employment.

        •   Any decision relating to full-time employment shall rest entirely with the Company
            and shall be subject to its internal policies, performance standards, and business
            needs.

    This Internship/Intern Training Period engagement shall not be construed as an offer,
    assurance, or entitlement to future employment with the Company under any circumstances.

    •   Completion Certificate

        Upon successful completion of the Internship or Intern Training Period, and subject to the
        fulfillment of all assigned roles and responsibilities, the Company may issue a Completion
        Certificate acknowledging the duration and nature of the engagement.

        Issuance of such Completion Certificate shall be subject to the following conditions:

            •   Successful completion of the prescribed program tenure.

            •   Satisfactory performance, conduct, and behavior throughout the engagement.

            •   Full compliance with the Company’s policies, confidentiality obligations, and
                completion of all exit formalities.

PERFORMANCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM

Introduction

The Performance Management System (PMS) is designed to establish a structured and continuous
process for evaluating employee performance in alignment with the Company’s objectives, values,
and business goals. The system aims to promote accountability, encourage continuous improvement,
and support employee development through regular performance assessments and feedback.

The PMS provides a fair and objective framework to measure individual contributions, identify
strengths and areas for improvement, and link performance outcomes with career growth, learning
opportunities, and rewards, wherever applicable. Performance evaluations under this system are
conducted in a transparent, merit-based, and consistent manner, while considering organizational
requirements and role expectations.

The Company reserves the right to modify, implement, or review the Performance Management
System at its discretion to ensure effectiveness, business alignment, and sustained organizational
growth.

Definitions

For the purpose of this policy:

    •   Performance Management System (PMS): A structured process for planning, monitoring,
        evaluating, and improving employee performance.
    •   Performance Improvement Plan (PIP): A formal, time-bound plan initiated to address
        performance gaps and provide structured support to enable improvement.
    •   Appraisal Cycle: The defined period during which employee performance is reviewed for
        appraisal and reward consideration.
    •   Reporting Manager: The immediate supervisor responsible for managing, evaluating, and
        providing feedback on an employee’s performance.
    •   Loss of Pay (LOP): Leave availed without pay, resulting in a proportional salary deduction
        for the applicable period.
    •   Probation: The initial employment period during which confirmation is subject to
        satisfactory performance.

Applicability

This Performance Management System is applicable to all full-time employees of the Company,
unless otherwise specified. Employees on probation, internship, or contractual engagement may
be covered under a separate evaluation process or as defined in their respective employment terms.

Participation in the Performance Management System is mandatory for all applicable employees and
forms an integral part of performance reviews, appraisals, and other employment-related decisions.

Documentation and Record Maintenance

All documentation related to PMS, including performance reviews, appraisal records, feedback, PIPs,
written notices, review meeting minutes, and outcomes, shall be formally documented and maintained
by the HR Department.

These records shall be retained for internal reference, compliance, audits, and decision-making
purposes and may be used in matters related to appraisals, disciplinary action, or separation, as
applicable.

Provisions:

1. Performance Evaluation Criteria

Employee performance shall be assessed based on, but not limited to, the following
  • Achievement of assigned goals and targets
  • Quality and timeliness of work
  • Skills, competency, and role effectiveness
  • Attendance, discipline, and adherence to Company policies
  • Collaboration, communication, and professional conduct
  • Demonstration of Company values and culture

2. Roles and Responsibilities

   -   Employee Responsibilities:
         • Actively participate in the PMS process
         • Work towards agreed goals and performance expectations
         • Seek and accept constructive feedback
         • Maintain professionalism and transparency during evaluations.

   -   Reporting Manager Responsibilities:
          • Set clear performance expectations and goals
          • Provide timely feedback and guidance
          • Conduct fair, objective, and unbiased evaluations
          • Recommend development plans and performance outcomes

   -   HR Responsibilities:
          • Facilitate and administer the PMS process
          • Ensure consistency, fairness, and confidentiality
          • Maintain records related to performance evaluations
          • Support employees and managers during the PMS cycle

3. Performance Cycle
    • Salary appraisals may be considered upon completion of one (1) year, i.e., 12 months of
       continuous service with the Company.
    • The appraisal process is entirely performance-driven and discretionary. The Company is
       not obligated to conduct appraisals at a fixed time or on a mandatory basis.
    • All information related to salary appraisals, increments, and compensation is strictly
       confidential and has a long-term impact on the Company’s working environment and culture.
    • Employees are expected to maintain confidentiality regarding their wages and appraisal
       outcomes as part of the performance review process.
    • Any discussion or disclosure of increments and/or salary hikes among colleagues is strictly
       prohibited. If such instances are observed, the Company may initiate strict disciplinary
       action against the concerned parties, which may include withdrawal of increment,
       reduction of the current CTC, or other appropriate action, as deemed necessary, for
       adversely affecting the Company’s work environment.
    • Approved increments, if any, shall be effective from the employee’s appraisal of month and
       date, upon completion of one year of service.

     Appraisal on Resignation During Appraisal Cycle

       •   In the event an employee submits their resignation during the appraisal cycle or at the
           time when their appraisal becomes due, the appraisal process shall be kept on hold.
       •   Due to the employee’s resignation shall not be initiated, processed, or finalized, and the
           employee shall not be eligible for any appraisal-related benefits, including salary
           revision, increment, or performance-based rewards.
       •   Any appraisal under such circumstances shall be considered null and void, and no
           retrospective or pro-rata appraisal benefits shall be applicable during the notice of period
           or resignation of tenure.
       •   The Company reserves the right to make the final decision in such cases based on
           business requirements and policy discretion.

4. Performance Feedback and Development

The PMS encourages continuous feedback and communication between employees and managers.
Based on performance outcomes, employees may be guided through:

    •   Skill development initiatives
    •   Training and learning opportunities
    •   Performance improvement plans (if required)

    Linkage to Appraisal and Rewards

        Performance outcomes under the PMS may be considered for:

        •   Salary appraisals and increments
        •   Promotions or role enhancements
        •   Recognition and rewards

All appraisal-related decisions remain at the sole discretion of the Company and are subject to
business needs and policy guidelines.



5. Performance Improvement Plan

The performance improvement plan is a key aspect of the Performance Management System in
FiftyFive Technologies. An important outcome of the employee's further professional development
and motivates him or her to continuously improve the performance. An important aspect is standard
and assists them to improve the same. This is achieved through the administration of the Performance
Improvement Plan.

A Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) may be initiated when an employee’s performance
consistently falls below the expected standards or when significant performance gaps are identified.

    A. Key aspects of the PIP include:
       • Clearly defined performance gaps and improvement areas
       • Specific, measurable goals and expectations
       • Support mechanisms such as training, coaching, or mentoring
       • A defined review period, typically ranging from 15 days to 90 days, as determined by
           the Company
       • Regular progress reviews and documented feedback.

B. Work Performance Definitions:

  Unsatisfactory Work Performance: Unsatisfactory Work Performance may include, but is
  not limited to, the following behaviors:

      •   Inability to complete assigned tasks or correct errors within a reasonable timeframe
      •   Inability or unwillingness to learn new tasks or skills or to work collaboratively
      •   Inability to exercise sound judgment
      •   Inability to receive, understand, or follow instructions or directions
      •   Unprofessional behavior as a team member or in a managerial role



  Average Work Performance: Average Work Performance may include, but is not limited to,
  the following behaviors:

      •   Inability to consistently complete all assigned tasks or correct errors within a
          reasonable timeframe
      •   Inconsistent willingness or ability to learn new tasks or collaborate
      •   Inability to consistently exercise good judgment
      •   Inability to fully receive, understand, or follow instructions or directions
      •   Unprofessional behavior as a team member or manager on more than one occasion.



  Satisfactory Work Performance: Satisfactory Work Performance may include, but is not
  limited to, the following behaviors:

      •   Ability to complete assigned tasks or correct errors within a reasonable timeframe
      •   Willingness and ability to learn new tasks or skills and work collaboratively
      •   Ability to exercise sound judgment
      •   Ability to receive, understand, and follow instructions or directions
      •   Professional behavior as a team member or in a managerial role.

C. Leave Clause During Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)

  •   During the Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) period, all leave balances as defined
      under the Leave Policy of FiftyFive Technologies, including monthly leave and
      additional leave entitlements, shall be kept on hold. This period is specifically intended
      for the employee to focus exclusively on performance improvement and meeting the
      defined expectations.
  •   Employees under an active PIP shall not be permitted to avail any type of leave during
      the PIP duration.
  •   In the event of genuine emergency situations, the employee may avail strictly on a Loss
      of Pay (LOP) basis, subject to prior approval from the Reporting Manager and the HR
      Department.
  •   Any LOP availed during the PIP period shall not be converted, adjusted, or reversed
      against Casual Leave, Privilege Leave, or any other leave balance, even after successful
      completion or closure of the PIP.
  •   Normal leave eligibility and balances shall be reinstated only after the formal closure of
      the PIP and subject to satisfactory performance improvement.



D. Pre-Performance Improvement Plan:

  Before initiating a formal PIP, the Reporting Manager must address performance concerns
  through informal discussions, guidance, and coaching. These discussions must be supported
  by documented evidence such as emails, feedback notes, or meeting records.

  If the informal approach does not result in satisfactory improvement, the Reporting Manager
  shall inform the HR Team, and the matter shall proceed to the formal PIP stage.

E. Initiation of Performance Improvement Plan

   Written Notice

   Once the formal PIP is initiated, the employee shall receive a written notice, with the
   Reporting Manager and HR Team involved. The notice shall clearly outline:

       •   Areas of improvement identified by the Reporting Manager
       •   Duration of the PIP, typically ranging between 15 to 90 days
            (The final decision on the PIP duration shall rest with the Reporting Manager, in
           consultation with HR)
       •   Applicable terms and conditions during the PIP period, including forfeiture of any
           bonus or incentive for the month
       •   Support measures to be provided, such as additional training, supervision, coaching,
           or peer support
       •   Consequences of failure to demonstrate improvement within the review period.




F. Conditions During the PIP Period

   •   Employees under an active PIP are not eligible to opt for or avail any type of leave
   •   Employees shall not be eligible for appraisal, salary increment, promotion, or bonus
       during the PIP period
   •   Employees are expected to strictly adhere to performance expectations and cooperate
       fully with the PIP process.


G. Performance Review Meeting

   At the end of the PIP review period, a Performance Review Meeting shall be conducted. The
   meeting shall be led by the Immediate Reporting Manager or Project Manager, and the
   Head of Human Resources shall also be present.

H. Outcomes of the Performance Review

  a) Satisfactory Improvement

        Potential Outcome:
        If the Reporting Manager determines that the employee has met the required
        performance standards, no further corrective action shall be taken, and the PIP shall
        be considered cleared.

        Action:
        The employee shall continue under observation for the next three (3) months to
        ensure sustained performance.



  b) Partial Improvement

        Potential Outcome:
        If significant improvement is observed and performance standards are likely to be met
        shortly, the PIP period may be extended.

        Action:

            •     Extension of the PIP shall be communicated in writing
            •     Revised terms and duration shall be clearly outlined
            •     Additional training or support may be recommended
            •     A new performance review meeting date shall be scheduled



  c) No Improvement / Insufficient Improvement

        Potential Outcome:
         If there is no overall improvement or performance that remains below the required
        standard, the matter shall be formally escalated to HR.

        Action:

            •     HR shall proceed with separation of the employee from the organization in
                  accordance with the Company’s separation policy.
            •     Final salary settlement and issuance of the Experience Letter shall be
                  governed by the applicable separation clause.
            •     The Company reserves the right to make the separation effective
                  immediately.

    I. PIP Provisions and Confidentiality
          • During the Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) period, employees shall not be
              eligible to avail any type of leave.
          • An employee may be issued a maximum of three (3) Performance Improvement
              Plans (PIPs) during their entire tenure with the Company.
          • Under no circumstances shall an employee be placed under a Performance
              Improvement Plan (PIP) more than three (3) times during their tenure with the
              Company. In the event that performance concerns continue to recur after the
              completion of three PIPs, the Company shall initiate strict corrective action, which
              may include disciplinary measures or separation from employment, in accordance
              with Company policy and applicable laws.
          • All records, communications, discussions, and outcomes related to the PIP process
              are strictly confidential and shall be handled in accordance with Company
              confidentiality standards.
          • All information, records, discussions, documentation, feedback, and outcomes related
              to the Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) process are strictly confidential. Such
              information shall be shared only on a need-to-know basis with the employee
              concerned, the Reporting Manager, the HR Team, and authorized management
              representatives.
          • Employees are strictly prohibited from disclosing, discussing, or sharing any PIP-
              related information with colleagues or unauthorized parties. Any breach of
              confidentiality may result in disciplinary action, which may include withdrawal of
              benefits, corrective measures, or separation from employment, in accordance with
              Company policy.



Disciplinary Action

Any misuse, misrepresentation, or manipulation of the PMS process, including influencing
evaluations or breaching confidentiality, may lead to disciplinary action, up to and including
withdrawal of appraisal benefits or other corrective measures.




Confidentiality

All performance-related information, including ratings, feedback, and appraisal outcomes, is strictly
confidential. Employees are expected to maintain confidentiality and refrain from discussing
performance reviews, ratings, or compensation details with colleagues.

Any breach of confidentiality may result in disciplinary action as per Company policy.

Non-Cooperation During PMS / PIP

Failure or refusal by an employee to actively participate in the Performance Management System or
cooperate during the Performance Improvement Plan process—including non-attendance of review
meetings, failure to follow instructions, or lack of effort toward improvement—may be treated as
non-compliance or misconduct.

Such behavior may result in accelerated corrective action, including extension of the PIP,
withholding of appraisal benefits, disciplinary action, or separation from employment, at the
Company’s discretion.




Impact on Confirmation / Probation (If Applicable)

For employees on probation, placement under a Performance Improvement Plan may result in
extension of the probation period, deferment of confirmation, or other corrective measures, as
deemed appropriate by the Company.

Confirmation of employment shall be subject to satisfactory performance and successful completion
of all performance requirements.
